Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
146 PM PST Sun Nov 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Periods of light valley rain and snow continue through tonight, 
  with minor travel impacts in the Sierra.

* Holiday travel will be most ideal Monday into Tuesday, disrupted 
  by another weaker storm Tuesday night or Wednesday. 

* Dry and mild weather is favored for Thanksgiving Day, with 
  additional storms possible next weekend and beyond. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

For the rest of today, model guidance shows an upper trough moving 
through the region. With this setup aloft, the region sees periods 
of snow showers through this evening with valley locations seeing 
rain mixed in during the afternoon. The 18Z run of the HRRR shows 
the best shower chances (30-60%) in areas along I-80, followed by a 
15-30% chance along the Sierra crest. Elsewhere, chances look to be 
around 15% or less. For snowfall totals, the forecast still calls 
for up to around 2 inches of new snow at the Sierra crest with a 
20-30% NBM probability of over 2 inches by Monday morning. 
Elsewhere in the Sierra and in the Sierra foothills, amounts range
between a trace to around 1 inch of snow. With afternoon snow 
levels around 5500 ft allowing for rain or a rain/snow mix during 
the bulk of the showers, little to no snowfall accumulation is 
expected in valley portions including the Reno-Sparks area. Shower
chances look to completely fade around midnight tonight. 
Following these showers: eastern Sierra Valleys could see 
freezing fog going into Monday morning, reducing visibilities in 
the area. Please use caution as traveling conditions could be 
hazardous in the region due to this potential fog and the recent 
snowfall.

On Monday into early Tuesday, forecast guidance shows a high 
pressure ridge moving through the western CONUS. This will bring dry 
conditions to region, signaling a safer travel window weather-wise 
for those with holiday plans, especially if they include commuting 
over the Sierra. But the pattern expects to change late Tuesday 
into Wednesday with models projecting another upper trough moving 
in behind the ridge. This will bring another wintry system to the 
region with snow chances returning to NE CA and the Sierra through
Wednesday afternoon. This system continues to trend drier with 
the Sierra crest now having a 20-60% NBM probability for 2+ inches
of snow and Sierra passes having a 30-50% NBM probability for 1+ 
inches by Wednesday evening. Spillover potential at this time 
looks limited though there is 15-25% chance for light showers in 
the Sierra Front. Forecast snow levels range begin around 
5000-5500 ft on Tuesday night, but rise to around 6000-6500 ft by 
late Wednesday afternoon. This may allow for valley areas that
experience showers to see rain over snow. Sierra ridge winds are 
also projected to increase Tuesday night with gusts up to around 
60-70 mph in the forecast. Please continue to watch for forecast 
updates on this system especially if you must travel through the 
Sierra late Tuesday into Wednesday as conditions may be hazardous 
once again.

Beyond the midweek system, ensemble guidance is showing another 
ridge moving over the western CONUS, which signals warmer and drier 
weather for Thanksgiving Day and Friday. Extended guidance continues 
to hint at another wetter and windier weather system over the 
following weekend, but details are uncertain this far out. -078

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: Generally VFR conditions expected today until 22/23Z
when there is a 20-40% chance for light rain/snow showers, which 
could reduce ceilings and visibility to MVFR conditions and cause 
potential mountain terrain obscurations. Shower chances then fade 
by around 23/07Z. Low clouds or patchy freezing fog near the 
terminal resulting in IFR conditions may be possible between 
23/07-15Z following the aforementioned showers, but chances remain
low (<10%) at this time.

Regional Outlook: Mostly VFR conditions for Sierra Front terminals 
(KCXP,KMEV) with a 20-40% chance of light rain/snow showers through 
23/07Z, which could reduce ceilings and visibility to MVFR 
conditions and cause potential mountain terrain obscurations. 
KTRK/KTVL see a 30-60% chance for light snow showers through 
23/06Z (minimal accumulations expected), causing MVFR conditions. 
As a result of the showers, the eastern Sierra Valleys (KTRK, 
KTVL) then sees freezing fog potential through around 23/19Z, 
which could cause LIFR conditions. VFR conditions are expected 
for KMMH with a 10-20% chance for light snow showers between 
23/00-06Z.

24-72 Hour Outlook: Dry conditions are anticipated for the region
on Monday into Tuesday. Sierra snow chances then return late 
Tuesday into Wednesday, causing potential aviation impacts for 
midweek holiday travel. -078
